title: MSK: managed Kafka, and when it beats Kinesis

videos.script: Kinesis is AWS's own stream. Kafka is the open-source one that most of the industry runs, and MSK is AWS running Kafka for you. {{two}} The ideas are the same ones you met in lesson 20, under other names. A shard is a partition. A sequence number is an offset. {{names}} But Kafka adds something Kinesis leaves to a library. A consumer group remembers where it stopped, on the broker. {{groups}} moto has no Kafka in it. So this lesson runs a real Kafka broker on your own machine, from the official release. You will see partitions, offsets, lag and a replay with your own eyes. {{broker}} Then the part one broker cannot show. Copies of every partition in three zones, and the settings that decide whether a write survives losing one. {{replicas}} And last, the question the title asks. You will price the same month on Kinesis and on MSK, and find where one starts to beat the other. {{price}}
